text: {"status":"unresolved","evidence_ids":["ev-ac49638f6133bbec20a681ad"],"request_dft":true,"proposed_test_ids":["relax-five-pilot-orderings-same-protocol"],"rationale":"The claim is comparative: ordering 01 must be the lowest of five cation orderings. The only record is a converged DFT static energy for ordering 01 (-9.35081491 eV/atom). Nothing is recorded for the other four orderings. Without their energies under the same protocol, the energy above the lowest pilot ordering cannot be computed, so a single absolute energy cannot show that ordering 01 sits at the 0.0 threshold. It also cannot show that another ordering is lower. The record is therefore admissible and well-converged in forces (0.00883 eV/A) and stress (0.3 kbar), but it does not cover the claim's comparative scope. The method signature also states that it was not independently convergence-tested. This adds some uncertainty to small energy differences between orderings, though it would affect all orderings similarly. No peers have spoken, so I have no peer claims to support or dispute yet. Assumption to expose: that all five orderings share the same cell size and composition (Nb4Ta4O20, 32 atoms), which would make per-atom energies comparable. Falsification test: relax all five orderings with the identical protocol (nbtao5-fixed-kmesh-v1). The claim is falsified if any other ordering has a lower energy per atom than ordering 01. It is supported if ordering 01 is lowest, with the margin judged against numerical noise at the meV/atom level. A DFT calculation can decide this, so I request the follow-up test."}
